subject: Prepay schedule: escrow recovery, co-term mechanics and early-exit options
messages:
From: Angela Park <angela.park@brightmed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, BrightMed Procurement <procurement@brightmed.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Prepay structure & early-exit questions for multi-year deal

Ben — thanks for the call this morning. We want to nail down how early termination refunds would work if BrightMed commits to a 3-year annual prepay with a 24-month ramp (year 1 50%, year 2 75%, year 3 100%). A few specific asks so we can brief finance and legal: 

- How do you handle refunds if we terminate after year 2? Is it pro-rata, amortized, or escrowed?
- For co-terming with existing contracts, can you align renewal dates without penalizing the outstanding prepay?
- What audit rights / reporting will we get to validate usage against committed units?

We'd like a short term sheet showing 2–3 recovery options and the arithmetic for each so our CFO can model the worst case. Please include any standard redline language Redwood expects for early exit and co-terming.

Thanks —
Angela Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
BrightMed Health

Attachments: none (please send term sheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Angela Park <angela.park@brightmed.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure & early-exit questions for multi-year deal

Hi Angela — good questions and thanks for the clear ramp detail. I've attached a concise proposal with three recovery patterns (amortized credit, escrow waterfall, and capped refund) and worked examples for your ramp. High level: 

Option A — Straight amortization (default): prepaid dollars are amortized monthly over the firm commitment term. On early termination, remaining unamortized balance is refunded to customer minus any consumed usage beyond committed units. Simple, predictable.

Option B — Escrow recovery (recommended for mid-size prepay): Redwood places the non-consumed portion of the up-front payment into a short-term escrow schedule; on termination we draw down per the matrix (fast recovery first 12 months, then taper). This reduces clawback spikes for customer while protecting Redwood.

Option C — Waterfall with co-term carve-out: if you co-term multiple Redwood products or merge with other vendors, we apply a co-term offset to avoid double-charging; excess prepay is refunded on a 12–24 month schedule.

Attached: BRIGHTMED_term_proposal_20270421.pdf with worked numbers. Also include a pricing workbook if you want line-by-line math.

Next steps — I can: (1) update the draft with your preferred recovery approach and exact dates, (2) circulate to legal for redlines, or (3) send for signature once we align. Which do you prefer?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: BRIGHTMED_term_proposal_20270421.pdf (proposal, 4 pages); pricing_workbook_BRIGHT-4521.xlsx (xls)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure & early-exit questions for multi-year deal

Ben — looped in Karthik for finance/legal guidance. Quick thoughts before we send a follow-up to BrightMed: 

- Prefer Option B (escrow recovery) for a ramped commitment — it smooths customer P&L while preserving Redwood economics. 
- We should define amortization cadence (monthly) and an explicit "Escrow Recovery Matrix" saying how much is recoverable by month after effective date.
- Co-terming should allow a single alignment event (customer-initiated) per renewal cycle; additional co-terms should be subject to pro-rated adjustments to prevent gaming.

Ben, add a short clause that: "Redwood will not seek clawback for usage that exceeds committed units during the ramp months; recovery only applies to unapplied prepaid balance." Keeps negotiations simple.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure & early-exit questions for multi-year deal

Adding finance detail and a sample recovery schedule (see attached matrix). Key recommended redlines: 

1) Define "Amortization Period" as the committed term (36 months) and amortize prepaid fees monthly.
2) Escrow Recovery Matrix: first 180 days refundable at 90%, 181–365 days at 60%, 366–730 days at 30%, beyond 730 days non-refundable (unless overridden by co-term adjustment).
3) Co-term mechanics: allow customer to request co-terming once per contract year; Redwood will apply prorated credits and adjust the amortization schedule accordingly.
4) Audit: customer may request one audit per 12 months with 30 days' notice; Redwood will provide usage reports and token-level breakdowns.

I've attached escrow_recovery_matrix.xlsx with a column for example numbers based on your 50/75/100 ramp. Ben, suggest we include a worked example for a termination on month 28.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Finance, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: escrow_recovery_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Angela Park <angela.park@brightmed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightMed Procurement <procurement@brightmed.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure & early-exit questions for multi-year deal

Ben / team — thanks for the thorough options and the matrix. We reviewed with our CFO and have two requested redlines before we can sign: 

1) Cap the escrow recovery aggressiveness: we will accept the matrix but request that the 1–180 day band be capped so the recoverable amount in that band cannot exceed 20% of total prepay. This prevents large short-term clawbacks after a single bad quarter.
2) Audit rights: add contractual language for a single annual audit with mutually agreed external auditor and 45 days' notice (instead of 30).

If you can incorporate those two changes and re-issue the term sheet, we can route to our legal for a last pass. Also ask that Redwood include a DocuSign link when ready for signature.

Regards —
Angela Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
BrightMed Health
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Angela Park <angela.park@brightmed.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, BrightMed Procurement <procurement@brightmed.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay structure & early-exit questions for multi-year deal

Angela — appreciate the clear feedback. We've accepted both asks: (1) added a cap limiting recoverable amount in 1–180 day band to 20% of total prepay; (2) updated audit language to one annual audit with 45 days' notice and mutually agreed auditor. 

I attached the updated term sheet (term_sheet_brightmed_v1.pdf) and the redlined pricing workbook. If that looks good to you, I'll send the DocuSign packet with the final statement of work. DocuSign (preview): https://app.docusign.com/BRIGHT-4521/prepare 

Proposed immediate next steps: 
- Angela/legal: confirm redlines are acceptable or provide edits by EOD Friday.
- Ben: will prepare DocuSign and include the escrow recovery matrix as an exhibit.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Best,
